name: When is it better to repair exterior wood rather than replace it completely?

mainEntity.name: When is it better to repair exterior wood rather than replace it completely?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repairing exterior wood is generally more cost-effective and efficient when the damage is localized and hasn't compromised the overall structural integrity of the component. If only a small section of a board is rotted or damaged, a patch or partial replacement can be a practical solution. However, if the damage is widespread, involves significant structural components, or recurring due to underlying issues like poor drainage, replacement might be the better long-term investment. Consider the extent of the damage; minor issues are suitable for repair.
acceptedAnswer.description: Repairing exterior wood is better for localized damage, while widespread structural issues often necessitate complete replacement.
